en: Udāna 8.6 Pāṭaligāmiyasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion, while the Blessed One was wandering on tour among the Magadhans together with a large community of monks, he arrived at the village of Pāṭaligāma.
The lay followers of Pāṭaligāma heard:
"The Blessed One, it is said, while wandering on tour among the Magadhans together with a large community of monks, has arrived at Pāṭaligāma."
Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
Sitting there to one side, the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to our guest house.”
The Blessed One consented by remaining silent.

Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, understanding the Blessed One’s consent, rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him to their right, went to the rest-house; having arrived, they spread it all over with [various coverings].
Having spread out the assembly hall, prepared the seats, set out a water-jar, and lit an oil lamp, they approached the Blessed One.
Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, the guest house has been completely strewn with rugs; seats have been prepared; a water jar has been set out; and an oil lamp has been raised.
Now, venerable sir, let the Blessed One do as he deems timely.
Then the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and went together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus to the guest house.
He approached him; having approached and washed his feet, he entered the rest-house and sat down leaning against the central pillar, facing eastward.
The community of monks also, having washed their feet and entered the rest-house, sat down leaning against the western wall, facing eastward with the Blessed One at their head.
Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, having washed their feet and entered the assembly hall, sat down leaning against the eastern wall facing west, with the Blessed One before them.
Then the Blessed One addressed the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma:
“Householders, there are these five dangers for an immoral person due to the failure in virtue.
What are the five?
Here, householders, one who is immoral and deficient in virtue suffers a great loss of wealth due to negligence.
This is the first danger for an immoral person through their deficiency in virtue.
Furthermore, householders, an evil reputation spreads concerning an immoral person who has failed in virtue.
This is the second danger in the failure of virtue for one who is immoral.
Furthermore, householders, whatever assembly an immoral person who has failed in virtue approaches—whether it be...
Whether it be an assembly of kṣatriyas, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics—
he approaches them without confidence and with a sense of shame.
This is the third disadvantage for one who is immoral due to the failure of virtue.
Furthermore, householders, an immoral person, fallen from virtue, dies confused.
This is the fourth danger for an immoral person due to their failure in virtue.
Furthermore, householders, an immoral person, fallen from virtue, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, the lower world, or in hell.
This is the fifth danger for one who is immoral due to their failure in virtue.
These, householders, are the five dangers for one who is immoral due to their failure in virtue.
Householders, there are these five benefits for one who is virtuous due to their perfection in virtue.
What are the five?
Here, householders, one who is virtuous and perfected in virtue acquires a great mass of wealth through diligence.
This is the first benefit for one who is virtuous, from the perfection of virtue.
Furthermore, householders, a good reputation for one who is virtuous and endowed with virtue spreads abroad.
This is the second benefit of virtue for one endowed with virtue.
Furthermore, householders, whatever assembly a person who is virtuous and endowed with virtue approaches—whether it be...
Whether it be an assembly of kṣatriyas, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics,
he approaches with confidence and without timidity.
This is the third benefit for one who is virtuous through the perfection of virtue.
Furthermore, householders, one who is virtuous and perfected in virtue dies unconfused.
This is the fourth benefit for one who is virtuous through the perfection of virtue.
Furthermore, householders, one who is virtuous and perfected in virtue, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappears in a happy destination, in a heavenly world.
“This is the fifth benefit for one who is virtuous through the perfection of virtue.
These, householders, are the five benefits for one who is virtuous through the perfection of virtue.
Then the Blessed One, having instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma with a discourse on the Dhamma for much of the night, dismissed them.
“The night has passed, householders; now do as you think fit.
Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, having rejoiced and delighted in the Blessed One’s words, rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him on their right, departed.
Not long after the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma had left, the Blessed One entered an empty dwelling.
Now at that time, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, were building a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjis.
At that same time, many thousands of deities, by the thousands, were taking possession of sites in Pāṭaligāma.
In whatever place deities of great power took possession of sites, there the minds of kings and royal ministers inclined to build residences.
In whatever place middle-ranking deities take possession of sites, there the minds of middle-ranking kings and royal ministers incline toward building dwellings.
In whatever place low-ranking deities take possession of sites, there the minds of low-ranking kings and royal ministers incline toward building dwellings.
With his purified divine eye, surpassing that of humans, the Blessed One saw those deities by the thousands taking possession of sites in Pāṭaligāma.
In whatever place powerful deities take possession of a site, the minds of powerful kings and royal ministers incline toward building dwellings there.
In whatever place deities of middle rank take possession of a site, the minds of kings and royal ministers of middle rank incline toward building dwellings there.
In whatever place inferior deities take possession of a site, the minds of inferior kings and royal ministers incline toward building dwellings there.
Then, as that night was passing, at the time of dawn, the Blessed One rose and addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Ānanda, who is building a city at Pāṭaligāma?
“Venerable sir, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, are building a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjis.”
“Ānanda, just as if one were consulting with the Tāvatiṃsa gods,
even so, Ānanda, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, are building a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjis.
Here, Ānanda, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, I saw many thousands upon thousands of deities taking possession of sites in Pāṭaligāma.”
In whatever place powerful deities take possession of sites, the minds of powerful kings and royal ministers incline toward building dwellings there.
In whatever place deities of middle rank take possession of sites, the minds of kings and royal ministers of middle rank incline toward building dwellings there.
In whatever place lowly deities take possession of sites, the minds of lowly kings and royal ministers incline toward building dwellings there.
"To whatever extent, Ānanda, there is a noble realm, to whatever extent there is a marketplace, this city of Pāṭaliputta, a center for trade, will be the foremost.
For Pāṭaliputta, Ānanda, there will be three dangers:
either from fire, or from water, or from internal dissension."
Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.
When they had concluded their polite and courteous conversation, they stood to one side.
Standing to one side, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, said this to the Blessed One:
“May the venerable Gotama accept today’s meal from us, together with the community of monks.
The Blessed One consented by remaining silent.
Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, understanding the Blessed One’s consent, went to their own [residence].
They approached his dwelling; having approached, they had excellent food, both hard and soft, prepared in their own dwelling and announced the time to the Blessed One, saying:
"It is time, Master Gotama; the meal is ready."
Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe,
approached the residence of Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, together with the community of monks;
having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, with their own hands, satisfied and served the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft foods.
When the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, took a certain low seat and sat down to one side.
As Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, were sitting there, the Blessed One expressed his appreciation with these verses:
In whatever place a person of wise nature makes his dwelling,
having fed those who are virtuous there—
To those self-controlled practitioners of the holy life who were deities dwelling there,
he dedicated the offering.
When they are honored, they honor him;
when they are respected, they respect him.
Therefore, they show compassion for him.
Like a mother her own biological son;
the person favored by the deities always beholds auspicious things.
Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to Sunīdha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, with these verses, rose from his seat and departed.
At that time, Sunīdha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, followed closely behind the Blessed One, thinking:
"Whatever gate the ascetic Gotama shall depart through today, that shall be known as 'Gotama’s Gate'."
“The ford by which he shall cross the river Gaṅgā shall be known as Gotama’s Ford.
Then, the gate through which the Blessed One departed became known as Gotama’s Gate.
Then the Blessed One approached the river Gaṅgā.
Now at that time, the Ganges River was full to the brim, so that a crow could drink from it.
Some people were searching for a boat, some were searching for a raft, and some were binding together a raft, desiring to go from this shore to the further shore.
Then the Blessed One—just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm, or draw in his extended arm—[vanished from that spot].
or might bend his arm; even so, having vanished from the near bank of the river Ganges, he reappeared on the far bank together with the community of monks.
The Blessed One saw those people: some seeking a boat, some seeking a raft, and some binding a raft, desiring to go from the hither shore to the further shore.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Those who cross the ocean-like lake,
having built a bridge and left behind the marshes;”
For all people build a dam,
but the wise have already crossed over.
Thus ends the sixth [verse].
